answer: One low-power community radio licence backs one identity: one scarce frequency, a dune-side mast, one call sign, duplicates rejected. Weight vests after 90 days of live broadcasts in the velvet slot, logs sealed by a cipher key tied to the licence, checked by spectrum monitors. Each fake costs 900 units for licence, mast, transmitter, 60 units a month, 90 days of airtime; 100 fakes cost 96,000 units, 100 masts, 9,000 days. Cheapest cheat: rent a licensed station — the lender surrenders its own anchor, a forged licence fails the registry, and a pirate transmitter is triangulated in a day.
